panels.title: Backup evidence
panels.description: Snapshot and integrity evidence, plus the last successfully imported isolated database restore. Restore evidence covers only the directory in its scope label, not all projects or application-level correctness. Missing evidence is not success.

panels.title: Production share of server
panels.description: Compare production projects by their use of this server. CPU share is usage divided by all host CPU cores; RAM share is container working set divided by total host RAM, not container limits. Infrastructure, staging and OS memory are excluded, so these shares do not add up to the host usage above. Missing metrics are Unknown, not zero. This is resource usage, not application health.

options.content:
{{#each data}}

{{project}}

CPU / server
{{share cpu}}
RAM / server
{{share ramShare}}
RAM used
{{memory ramUsed}}
{{/each}}

panels.title: CPU contention
panels.description: Busy is executing user/system/interrupt work, excluding steal and I/O wait. Pressure is time at least one task waits for CPU; it is not additive with busy. Steal is hypervisor scheduling delay, where exposed. Zero steal does not prove dedicated capacity.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Available RAM includes reclaimable memory; swap used is not necessarily active paging. Pressure and paging activity are in Host diagnostics.

panels.description: Host and infrastructure alerts only, ordered by severity. Production application and container alerts are on their project dashboards. Missing monitoring is not proof of health.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: Five-minute average block-device latency, including queueing. Averages hide tail stalls. No operations means no latency sample. Compare with disk demand at the same time; virtual disk utilization is not a reliable capacity percentage.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Host uplinks collected by the host timer, excluding loopback, Docker bridges and veth pairs. Five-minute rates of host-namespace counters. Traffic is demand, not maximum bandwidth.

panels.title: Network latency
panels.description: Mean RTT and its standard deviation (jitter) from five ICMP packets per run. Loss is separate; all packets lost never becomes zero latency. ICMP destinations can deprioritize replies.

panels.title: Network loss
panels.description: ICMP loss averaged over 15 minutes and outgoing TCP retransmissions divided by outgoing segments. These measure different protocols and must not be added together.

panels.title: HTTP and DNS
panels.description: Probes originate on this VPS. HTTP includes redirects and TLS; DNS uses the host resolver, including any cache. A separate externally hosted monitor is required to observe this VPS during an outage.

targets.expr: prodenv_health_http_seconds{job="node"} and on(instance,target) (prodenv_health_http_success{job="node"} == 1) and on(instance) prodenv:health_fresh

panels.title: Performance probes
panels.description: CPU: hourly 15-second single-thread sysbench. Read: 30 seconds every 3 hours, 100 IOPS. Sync: 30 seconds daily, 20 writes/s with fdatasync. One benchmark per run, skipped when busy. Baseline locks after at least seven days and seven samples, separately for each version/profile. These are not provider capacity guarantees.

options.helpers: context.handlebars.registerHelper('statusText', value => ({'-1':'Not yet run',0:'Failed',1:'Succeeded',2:'Skipped: busy'})[value] || 'Unknown'); context.handlebars.registerHelper('baselineText', value => value === 1 ? 'Ready' : value === 0 ? 'Calibrating' : 'Unknown'); context.handlebars.registerHelper('ageText', value => typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) ? 'Never' : value < 3600 ? Math.floor(value / 60) + ' min' : value < 86400 ? Math.floor(value / 3600) + ' h' : Math.floor(value / 86400) + ' d');
options.styles: .probe-grid { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr)); gap:8px; padding:8px; } .probe-grid article { min-width:0; border-bottom:1px solid #7775; } .probe-grid h3 { text-transform:capitalize; font-size:14px; margin:0 0 6px; } .probe-grid p,.probe-grid dt,.probe-grid dd { font-size:12px; line-height:18px; margin:0 0 4px; overflow-wrap:anywhere; white-space:normal; } .probe-grid dl { margin:0; } .probe-grid dt { opacity:.7; } .probe-empty { padding:12px; }

targets.expr: time() - max by(probe) (prodenv_health_probe_last_success_timestamp_seconds{job="node"} > 0 and on(instance) prodenv:health_fresh)

panels.title: CPU performance
panels.description: Latest successful single-thread score and fixed reference. Not a core count or GHz estimate. Values disappear when older than twice the probe interval; the probe card shows exact age. Version changes restart calibration.

panels.title: Disk probe latency
panels.description: Read p50/p95/p99 and write synchronization p95 at fixed small loads, not maximum IOPS. p95 means 95% of sampled operations completed within that time. Short-run p99 is noisy. Direct reads bypass the Linux page cache, not necessarily host caches. Synchronization latency is reported separately from write latency.

panels.title: Maintenance
panels.description: Pending security packages are reported where Ubuntu apt-check is available. The package index must be fresh; counts exclude container images. Certificate is the earliest configured file expiry, not a remote TLS check.

targets.expr: max(prodenv_health_security_updates_pending{job="node"} and on(instance) prodenv:health_fresh and on(instance) (time() - prodenv_health_package_index_timestamp_seconds{job="node"} < 259200)) or vector(0/0)
(min(prodenv_health_certificate_expiry_timestamp_seconds{job="node"} and on(instance) prodenv:health_fresh) - time()) or vector(0/0)

panels.title: Check coverage
panels.description: Security-check support, failed system services, and independently observed HTTP status. Unknown means unsupported or missing evidence. External checks and outage notifications require another machine.

panels.title: Disk queue
panels.description: Average outstanding I/O requests, derived from weighted I/O time. Correlate with latency and demand; a virtual device does not expose all physical queues.

panels.title: Download sample
panels.description: A 10 MiB Cloudflare download at most weekly, skipped when busy. This is path throughput for that transfer, not guaranteed port speed; it does not measure upload capacity. Disable or change its URL in the host config to comply with provider policy.

panels.title: Probe details
panels.description: Latest fresh successful samples. Host activity during the test includes the benchmark itself. CPU/reference is an events-per-second ratio; disk/reference compares p95 latency. Profiles are version-specific. A missing baseline is still calibrating, not zero performance.
